question: This LRU example has 4 slots and the access sequence A B C D E D F (the number in brackets is the time of last use). Why does E replace A, why does F replace B, and how many hits and misses are there?
reference_answer: A, B, C, D fill the four empty slots (4 misses). E (t=4) misses with the cache full, so the least recently used block is evicted: A, last used at 0. D at t=5 is a hit: nothing is evicted, D's time of last use is updated from 3 to 5. F (t=6) misses; now the least recently used is B (1) (C=2, E=4, D=5), so F replaces B. Final contents E(4), F(6), C(2), D(5). Total: 6 misses (A, B, C, D, E, F) and 1 hit (D), hit ratio 1/7.

checks.name: e_evicts_a
checks.description: E replaces A because A (time 0) is the least recently used.

checks.name: d_hit_updated
checks.description: The second access to D is a hit and D's last-use time is updated (3 -> 5).

checks.name: f_evicts_b
checks.description: F replaces B, which (time 1) is now the least recently used.

checks.name: six_misses
checks.description: 6 misses (A, B, C, D, E, F).
